clue.text: One child in a ring displaying martial art

indicators.note: the words one child sit in the middle of the words a ring

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
one is the Roman numeral I
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster in a training circle shows off a Japanese fighting skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese discipline of self-defence using throws and holds.

clue.text: Exercises aviators, requiring no indication of excellence necessarily

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercises

indicators.note: requiring no means the following letters must be removed from the aviators

parts.note: the Air Force is the body of military aviators
A1 (written AI) is a mark of top quality

explanation.surface: A training regime for pilots that must do without any badge of distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring no' takes AI (A1, top grade) out of AIR FORCE, leaving RFORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is a slightly old-fashioned adverb meaning by necessity, unavoidably.

clue.text: English city councillor with yarn about American

indicators.note: the councillor's letters go about, or around, the American

parts.note: lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread

explanation.surface: A local politician tells a story concerning an American, in some northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like a tale but is the thread LISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria in the far north-west of England, near the Scottish border.

clue.text: Second Star of Africa or India?

definitions.meaning: the Cullinan II diamond, set in the Imperial State Crown, is a gem in the royal crown
India was called the most precious possession of the British Empire

explanation.walkthrough: The Second Star of Africa is the Cullinan II diamond in Britain's Imperial State Crown; India was the proudest possession of the British Empire, so both are its most prized part.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the most valuable item in a collection, and is literally true of a diamond set in a crown.

clue.text: Fighting identified with crater?

definitions.meaning: the sport of fist fighting in a ring
a crater, read as one who crates, is engaged in packing things into boxes

explanation.walkthrough: 'crater' wants to be a hole in the ground, but here it is someone who puts goods into crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing is fighting with fists; it is also the act of packing items into containers.

clue.text: Fuel favoured a lot of motion on wheels

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in a teacher's pet

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so a final letter goes

parts.note: a roll is movement on wheels

explanation.surface: Car fuel is the favourite thing for keeping wheels turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims ROLL to ROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol is the British word for gasoline, a motor fuel.

clue.text: Article in the main elevated tense European art lover?

indicators.note: the article sits in the middle of the other pieces
in a down clue, elevated means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A tense European lover of art writes an article at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is a poetic name for the sea; in a down entry 'elevated' reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person devoted to beauty, especially in the arts.

clue.text: Libertine accepting dessert and cold snack item

indicators.note: the libertine takes in, or accepts, the other pieces

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man
an ice is a frozen dessert
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A womaniser takes pudding and a cold bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice cake is a light crisp disc of puffed rice eaten as a snack.

clue.text: Lord's debutant role? Old member of Lords welcoming new

indicators.note: the peer welcomes, or takes in, the new letter

parts.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: An elderly peer welcomes a newcomer to the House of Lords for a first appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's here is the London cricket ground, not the upper house; the opener is a batsman who goes in first.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the opening batsman is the first to make their debut at the crease in an innings.

clue.text: Engineer brought back fabrication having received slimmed-down offer

indicators.note: the reversed fabrication has received the trimmed offer inside it
brought back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lie is a fabrication

indicators.note: slimmed down means the word offer loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: An engineer backs out of a fabricated story after getting a reduced bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' gives EIL from LIE; 'slimmed-down' leaves FFE from offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Eiffel was the French civil engineer behind the Paris tower bearing his name.

clue.text: Months one's invested in energy framework? Try another place

indicators.note: the months and one are put inside the other pieces

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a grate is a framework of bars
M is an abbreviation for month
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A long-term investment in an energy framework fails, so you move on elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle and try life somewhere else.

clue.text: Beneficial hours in working in Government

indicators.note: working signals the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Putting in long hours in a Whitehall job is good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges HOURS IN to NOURISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nourishing does you good, as healthy food sustains the body.

clue.text: Nothing recalled about English legal right

indicators.note: the reversed nothing goes about, or around, the English
recalled means called back, so read in reverse

parts.note: nil is nothing

explanation.surface: No one remembers anything about English law on rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a right to keep someone's property until a debt they owe is paid.

clue.text: Unexciting cinematography only partly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse
only partly means just some of the word's letters are used

explanation.surface: A film's camera work was dull, and only partly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only partly' picks EMAT from cinEMATography and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame describes something dull and lacking excitement or spirit.

clue.text: Italian motorcyclist qualified, covering section in main road

indicators.note: the inner pieces go in the main road

parts.note: the A1 (written AI) is Britain's main road north from London

indicators.note: the qualified phrase covers, or encloses, the section

parts.note: got in means qualified, as for a team or a course

explanation.surface: An Italian biker qualifies, covering one stretch of the trunk road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Agostini is the Italian rider who won fifteen Grand Prix world titles.

clue.text: Praise work I abandoned, taken on by former partner

indicators.note: the remainder is taken on by, attached after, the ex

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter I is left out

parts.note: toil is hard work

explanation.surface: Praise for work that was dropped and picked up by an ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes I from TOIL, giving TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly and enthusiastically.

clue.text: Approach to harbour and nothing more expressed in three lines

indicators.note: these words are put in between the line letters

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so three lines are three Ls
sweet FA is slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Coming into port, with nothing more to say, in a three-line poem.
explanation.walkthrough: AND and FA go in among three Ls: L, then ANDFA, then LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A landfall is the first sight of land, or arrival at land, after a voyage.

clue.text: Support only half the letters?

indicators.note: only half means just the back half of the word for all the letters is kept

parts.note: the alphabet is the set of all letters

explanation.surface: A teacher gives help with only half of the ABC.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: ________ isn't represented on a lot of maps!

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, rearranged
a lot of means most but not all, so a letter goes

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

explanation.surface: A mythical place is missing from most maps, as the blank invites you to fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts ATLAS to ATLA; 'represented' shuffles that with ISNT. The blank is the definition, and the completed sentence is true.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary sunken island of Plato's tale, which fits the blank because no real map shows it.

clue.text: Whole of one's foot or half of one's foot, initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each word is used

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether something is all of a foot or half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: For a horse, its whole foot is the hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoof is the horny foot of a horse or similar animal.

clue.text: Old money I extracted from the Pope?

indicators.note: extracted means the letter I is pulled out

parts.note: Francis is the papal name of the recent pontiff

explanation.surface: A cash sum removed from the Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Francs were the currency of France and Belgium before the euro.

clue.text: Solar phenomenon given fresh angle possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A sunny effect seen from a new viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A green flash is a brief green spot glimpsed at sunset or sunrise.

clue.text: Performances seen around old time joints

indicators.note: the performances go around the other pieces

parts.note: gigs are performances by musicians

explanation.surface: Shows held in seedy old nightspots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' looks like bars or clubs; it is cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a leg of lamb or mutton, a joint of meat.

clue.text: Sausage? Setter's looking up after reduction in vegetarian fare

indicators.note: the setter's piece comes after the shortened salad
a reduction in means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a salad is a meatless dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the setter says I'm, I am

explanation.surface: The setter turns to meat after a cut-back diet of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduction in' trims SALAD to SALA; 'looking up' turns IM into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a highly seasoned cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: Alien forest worker, say, is someone from outside France

parts.note: ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial
a ranger patrols a forest

explanation.surface: A foreign woodland patrolman, as seen from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the ranger as one example of a forest worker. Étranger is French for foreigner.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a foreigner, someone not from France.

clue.text: A lot of excellent beer is the last thing you want?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: fine means excellent
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Drinking lots of fine beer is the last thing you need.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'something unwelcome', but means the final item.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing section of a show, the final part of it.

clue.text: Number getting cold aboard fixed Arctic vehicle?

indicators.note: the other pieces climb aboard, inside, the fixed word

parts.note: sat means stayed fixed in one place

explanation.surface: A number of people turn cold aboard a stuck polar vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A snocat is a tracked motor vehicle for travelling over snow.

clue.text: Film composer one morning seen amongst leaves

indicators.note: these pieces are seen among, inside, the leaves

parts.note: a person leaves property in their wills
one is the Roman numeral I
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: A movie composer is spotted among the leaves one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' is a verb, as one leaves things in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: John Williams is the American composer of the Star Wars and Jaws scores.
